findings.text: The manifest reads status: complete but carries no tests line, no test_logs, and neither suite arm: crew check --manifest --run r-20261118T062615707658-qwnw-red-file-a-claimless-review-is-refused-at-store exits 1 with 'status is complete but no test result is recorded', 'status is complete but baseline_suite is missing', 'status is complete but after_suite is missing' and 'messages_received: no delivery receipt was recorded, so the manifest must say `messages_received: none`'. The done_when's requirements that the manifest list each cause with a verdict and carry both arms as inline JSON with full 40-character revisions are therefore unmet in the record promotion reads; the arms exist only as tripwire JSON inside the worker's own session bash logs (omp-home/agent/sessions/.../93.bash.log and 124.bash.log), and the file is the 11-line orientation write with checkpoint 'manifest being finalized', so the record was never closed.

The closing paragraph says 'the head gate re-run and the base attempt are named by the manifest's test_logs and negative_control_log', but both fields are absent from the manifest (test_logs parses to [] and there is no negative_control_log line), so the committed evidence's only pointer to its own logs dangles and a reader cannot reach scoped-gate-1795061275094737226.log or logs/negctl-base.log from the fragment. The same repair that fills the manifest answers this finding.

The table lists 'negative control, base test file' (line 26) and 'node tests, base' (line 29) as two arms at 42fe90d0 with identical 2 failed / 2 passed / EXIT=1 results, but only one log at that revision exists on disk (logs/negctl-base.log), so one measurement is presented as two; and neither row carries the failing test ids the done_when asks to be logged beside the head run, which is where a reader would look for them rather than in the uncommitted run directory.

notes: Scores are per dimension and independent. Durability: the diff adds no assertion, so the guard is the pre-existing pair at tests/test_a_claimless_review_is_refused_at_store.py:114 (assert len(findings) == 1) and :128 (assert exit_code == 0); reinstating the regression -- removing the fixture's messages_received line -- reddens exactly those two ids and nothing else, which logs/negctl-base.log records at 42fe90d0 with EXIT=1, and which I reproduced independently in this review worktree as '2 failed, 2 passed in 1.09s'. No assertion in the diff compares a value against a variable the test itself passed in, because the diff adds none. added_failure_count 0 is derived from the reviewed run's own arms: baseline_suite-1795060525175189575.log at 42fe90d0 and after_suite-1795060600274873296.log at afd2113b both record '58 passed' with EXIT=0 over tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py and tests/test_every_shared_home_lock_holds_across_nodes.py, so failure_ids are empty on both sides and the delta is zero (the earlier pair, baseline_suite-1795060023008913837.log and after_suite-1795060068180595785.log, reads the same 58 passed / EXIT=0). Reuse: the diff adds no function, class or module, so no capability is forked; the one rule it leans on, that a run with no delivery receipt must state messages_received: none, is owned by reckon/hooks/worker_inbox.py:57 and the fixture states it rather than restating the check. Fit: the fixture line continues the same f-string the test already writes, but the fragment departs from the sibling idiom in docs/evidence/fragments/queued-work-needs-no-workaround/, for example qwnw-a-commit-keyed-list-item-is-read-codex-negative-control.html, which embeds the raw log in a pre block with its failing ids.
